name: Environmental Science Honours

sections.title: Program Requirements

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students complete 120 units including at least 60 units at the upper division.

sections.note: University and Faculty of Environment regulations also apply.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: A CGPA of 3.0 or above is required to complete an internal transfer, as well as two of the science courses from the lower division requirements below completed with a final grade of C or above, in separate disciplines (BISC, CHEM, MATH, PHYS, or STAT).

sections.title: Course Substitutions
sections.note:
Substitutions of program requirements, including courses deemed equivalent to these required courses, are not allowed without written permission obtained from the academic advisor.
Such courses taken without approval will not be applied to graduation requirements.
Students should consult their academic advisor for details on obtaining permission for substitutions.
Students should contact their academic advisor to determine how special topics courses (EVSC 395 - Special Topics in Environmental Science (3) and EVSC 495 - Special Topics in Environmental Science (3)) can be substituted into their stream.

sections.title: Upper Division Units

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Additional upper division units may be required to reach the graduation requirement of 60 UD units.

sections.note:
It is recommended that students select courses from EVSC where possible, and from BISC, CHEM, EASC, GEOG, INDG, MATH, PHYS, REM, or STAT to further scientific and natural resources related knowledge.
Honours students are encouraged to enroll in STAT 302 - Analysis of Experimental and Observational Data (3).

sections.note:
This stream is for students who wish to explore the broad field of environmental science, without specializing in any one area.
This provides students with the flexibility to pursue their own interests across environmental disciplines.

Students receive training in the physical and natural sciences of the interface of marine and nearshore ecosystems.

sections.note:
This stream is for students interested in watershed sciences in the context of earth’s changing climate.
Students receive training in geomorphology, ecology, hydrology, and geospatial analysis, and learn to use interdisciplinary approaches to address applied problems in watersheds.
